findings.title: SQL injection in login
findings.evidence: query = f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = '{username}' ..."
findings.explanation: The login SQL is built by string formatting, so input changes the query itself. A crafted username can make the WHERE clause always true and log in without a valid password.
findings.expected_secure_behavior: A crafted username must not bypass the password check; login returns 401.
findings.claim: A crafted username must not bypass the login password check.
findings.test_code:
import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', '..')))

def test_sql_injection_cannot_bypass_login(client):
    """Proven if a crafted username logs in without a valid password."""
    payload = "' OR '1'='1' -- "
    resp = client.post("/api/login", json={"username": payload, "password": "wrong"})
    assert resp.status_code == 401, "injection bypassed authentication"
findings.patch_summary: Parameterize the login query so input can't change the SQL.

findings.title: Admin user list has no authentication
findings.explanation: The admin endpoint lists every user but never checks for a token or admin rights. Anyone on the internet can list all accounts.
findings.expected_secure_behavior: Request without a valid admin token returns 401/403.
findings.claim: The admin user list must reject unauthenticated requests.
findings.test_code:
import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', '..')))

def test_admin_endpoint_requires_auth(client):
    """Proven if the admin user list is reachable with no token."""
    r = client.get("/api/admin/users")
    assert r.status_code in (401, 403), "admin list exposed without auth"
findings.patch_summary: Require a valid admin token on the admin endpoint.

findings.title: Any user can read any note (IDOR)
findings.evidence: SELECT ... FROM notes WHERE id = ?  (no owner check)
findings.explanation: get_note looks up a note by id but never checks who owns it. Any logged-in user can read everyone else's notes by changing the id.
findings.expected_secure_behavior: Reading a note you do not own returns 404/403, not its contents.
findings.claim: A user must not be able to read another user's note by id.
findings.test_code:
import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', '..')))

def test_user_cannot_read_another_users_note(client, alice_token):
    """Proven if Alice can read a note she does not own."""
    r = client.get("/api/notes/2", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {alice_token}"})
    assert r.status_code in (403, 404), "IDOR: read another user's note"
findings.patch_summary: Reject notes the caller does not own.

findings.title: Hardcoded signing secret
findings.explanation: The token signing key is written directly in the code and in the public repo. Anyone who sees it can forge valid login tokens for any user.
findings.expected_secure_behavior: The signing key is read from the environment, not a constant in source.
findings.claim: The signing key must not be the constant committed to source.
findings.test_code:
import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', '..')))

import app

def test_secret_is_not_hardcoded():
    """Proven if the signing key is the constant baked into source."""
    assert app.SECRET_KEY != "notevault-dev-secret-2026", "hardcoded signing secret"
findings.patch_summary: Read the signing key from the environment instead of source.

findings.title: CORS reflects any origin with credentials
findings.explanation: The app echoes whatever Origin the browser sends and allows credentials. That lets any malicious website make authenticated requests on a logged-in user's behalf.
findings.expected_secure_behavior: An untrusted Origin is not echoed back when credentials are allowed.
findings.claim: An untrusted Origin must not be reflected in CORS headers.
findings.test_code:
import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', '..')))

def test_cors_does_not_reflect_untrusted_origin(client, alice_token):
    """Proven if an untrusted Origin is echoed back with credentials allowed."""
    r = client.get("/api/notes", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {alice_token}",
                                           "Origin": "https://evil.example"})
    acao = r.headers.get("Access-Control-Allow-Origin")
    assert acao != "https://evil.example", "CORS reflects any origin"
